skill.name: security-checklist
skill.description: Review application security with OWASP guidance, secure coding examples, automated scan workflows, authentication patterns, and compliance checklists.
skill.summary: Apply a structured security review across code, dependencies, authentication, configuration, and operations.
skill.author: AI Agent Hub

security_audit.summary: All 141 static detections are false positives caused by Markdown syntax, defensive checklists, or intentionally vulnerable and remediated examples. No executable payload, prompt injection, credential collection, or exfiltration logic was found. Separate risks remain around automatic scans, unpinned tool installation, and active tests without explicit authorization boundaries.

remediation.issue: Security scans may run automatically without user confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: Require approval before every command, explain expected network and file access, and show the exact command before execution.

remediation.issue: Tool installation commands do not pin immutable versions.
remediation.suggestion: Pin reviewed versions or image digests, verify publisher signatures and checksums, and separate installation from normal audit execution.

remediation.issue: Active test payloads lack explicit scope and authorization controls.
remediation.suggestion: Require written authorization, defined targets, and a staging environment before privilege, injection, SSRF, or cloud metadata tests.

content.user_title: Audit Applications with an OWASP Security Checklist
content.value_statement: Security reviews can miss common vulnerabilities and inconsistent controls. This skill provides structured OWASP checks, secure examples, and scanning workflows for repeatable assessments.
actual_capabilities: Reviews designs and code against the OWASP Top 10.
Compares insecure and secure patterns for Python, JavaScript, SQL, sessions, and JWT handling.
Provides commands for npm audit, pip-audit, Semgrep, Bandit, TruffleHog, and Trivy.
Builds checklists for authentication, authorization, input validation, headers, logging, and secrets.
Summarizes GDPR and SOC 2 control considerations for engineering teams.
limitations: It provides guidance, not a complete penetration test or formal certification.
Scanning tools must be installed separately and may require network access.
Examples need adaptation for each framework, threat model, and deployment environment.
Active tests must run only on systems you are authorized to assess.

use_cases.title: Review a New Feature
use_cases.description: Check access control, validation, data handling, and error behavior before merging a feature.

use_cases.title: Standardize Security Reviews
use_cases.description: Apply consistent OWASP evidence and remediation criteria across repository reviews.

use_cases.title: Add Pipeline Scanning
use_cases.description: Select dependency, static analysis, secret, and container scans for delivery pipelines.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Basic Checklist Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this feature against the quick-start checklist. List missing controls, evidence, severity, and practical fixes. Ask for any context you need.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner wants a structured review of one feature.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Authentication Security
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this authentication flow for OWASP risks. Check password storage, sessions, MFA, rate limits, account enumeration, and authorization. Prioritize findings.
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer is reviewing login and session behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Repository Scanning
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a security scan plan for this repository. Select relevant dependency, SAST, secret, and container tools. Do not install or run tools without approval.
prompt_templates.scenario: A team needs repeatable automated security checks.

prompt_templates.title: Perform a Threat-Focused Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this architecture and supplied code. Map findings to OWASP categories, cite evidence, challenge assumptions, and propose verified remediations.
prompt_templates.scenario: An experienced reviewer needs an evidence-based assessment.

output_examples.input: Review a profile endpoint that accepts a user ID.
output: High: Verify resource ownership before returning profile data.
Medium: Use a parameterized query and validate the identifier format.
Evidence needed: route authorization tests for another user's identifier.

output_examples.input: Create a security scan plan for a Python service.
output: Run pip-audit for dependencies after approval.
Run Bandit for Python security patterns.
Record tool versions, exit codes, findings, and reviewed false positives.

output_examples.input: Assess a server feature that fetches user-provided URLs.
output: High: Enforce a hostname allowlist and block private or metadata ranges.
Disable redirects or validate every redirect target.
Set strict timeouts and isolate the fetch service from internal networks.

best_practices: Provide architecture, framework, data classification, and trust boundaries before review.
Confirm permission before running tools, and use the least privileges required.
Validate automated findings manually and record reproducible evidence for each decision.
anti_patterns: Do not run active payloads against unauthorized or production systems.
Do not install unpinned tools or apply automated fixes without review.
Do not treat checklist completion as proof that a system is secure.

faq.question: What does this skill review?
faq.answer: It covers OWASP risks, authentication, authorization, validation, headers, logging, secrets, dependencies, and selected compliance controls.

faq.question: Does it run security tools automatically?
faq.answer: The source includes automatic scan workflows. Review each command and grant explicit approval before execution.

faq.question: Which languages does it support?
faq.answer: Examples focus on Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, SQL, shell workflows, and language-independent security design.

faq.question: Does it provide compliance certification?
faq.answer: No. It summarizes selected GDPR and SOC 2 considerations but does not replace legal advice or an independent audit.

faq.question: Can it replace a penetration test?
faq.answer: No. It supports review and planning but cannot replace an authorized assessment by qualified security professionals.

faq.question: How should false positives be handled?
faq.answer: Verify each result against code and runtime context. Record the evidence and rationale before accepting or dismissing it.
